title: KCET 2024 Physics
subject: physics
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column C4

questions.q: The ratio of molar specific heats of oxygen is
questions.explanation: $\gamma = 1 + 2/f$; for a diatomic gas like O$_2$, $f=5$, so $\gamma = 1+2/5 = 1.4$.

questions.q: For a particle executing simple harmonic motion (SHM), at its mean position
options: Velocity is zero and acceleration is maximum
Velocity is maximum and acceleration is zero
Both velocity and acceleration are maximum
Both velocity and acceleration are zero
questions.explanation: At the mean position ($y=0$), $v=\omega\sqrt{A^2-y^2}$ is maximum while $a=-\omega^2y$ is zero.

questions.q: A motor-cyclist moving towards a huge cliff with a speed of 18 kmh$^{-1}$, blows a horn of source frequency 325 Hz. If the speed of sound in air is 330 ms$^{-1}$, the number of beats heard by him is
questions.explanation: The reflected frequency is $f''=f\dfrac{V+V_s}{V-V_s}$; with $V_s=5\,ms^{-1}$, $V=330\,ms^{-1}$, the beats $=f''-f=\dfrac{325\times2\times5}{325}=10$.

questions.q: A body has a charge of $-3.2\mu C$. The number of excess electrons it has is
questions.explanation: $n=\dfrac{Q}{e}=\dfrac{3.2\times10^{-6}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}=2\times10^{13}$ excess electrons.

questions.q: A point charge A of $+10\mu C$ and another point charge B of $+20\mu C$ are kept 1m apart in free space. The electrostatic force on A due to B is $\vec F_1$ and the electrostatic force on B due to A is $\vec F_2$. Then
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the force on A due to B is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force on B due to A.

questions.q: A uniform electric field $E=3\times10^5\,NC^{-1}$ is acting along the positive Y-axis. The electric flux through a rectangle of area $10\,cm\times30\,cm$ whose plane is parallel to the Z-X plane is
questions.explanation: Since the plane is parallel to the Z-X plane, its normal is along Y, so $\phi=E\times A=3\times10^5\times(0.1\times0.3)=9\times10^3\,Vm$.

questions.q: The total electric flux through a closed spherical surface of radius 'r' enclosing an electric dipole of dipole moment 2aq is (Give $\varepsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)
questions.explanation: A dipole has zero net enclosed charge, so by Gauss's law the total flux through any closed surface enclosing it is zero.

questions.q: Under electrostatic condition of a charged conductor, which among the following statements is true?
options: The electric field on the surface of a charged conductor is $\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$, where $\sigma$ is the surface charge density
The electric potential inside a charged conductor is always zero
Any excess charge resides on the surface of the conductor
The net electric field is tangential to the surface of the conductor
questions.explanation: Since the field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is zero, any excess charge resides entirely on its surface.

questions.q: A cube of side 1 cm contains 100 molecules each having an induced dipole moment of $0.2\times10^{-6}\,C-m$ in an external electric field of $4\,NC^{-1}$. The electric susceptibility of the materials is _____ $C^2N^{-1}m^{-2}$

A capacitor of capacitance $5\mu F$ is charged by a battery of emf 10V. At an instant of time, the potential difference across the capacitors is 4V and the time rate of change of potential difference across the capacitor is $0.6\,Vs^{-1}$. Then the time rate at which energy is stored the capacitor at the instant is
questions.explanation: $u=\dfrac12CV^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dt}=CV\dfrac{dV}{dt}=5\times10^{-6}\times4\times0.6=12\mu W$.

questions.q: $\vec E$ is the electric field inside a conductor whose material has conductivity $\sigma$ and resistivity $\rho$. The current density inside the conductor is $\vec j$. The correct form of Ohm's law is
questions.explanation: From $V=iR$, $\dfrac{V}{\ell}=\dfrac{i}{A}\rho$, which gives $\vec E=\rho\vec j$.

questions.q: In the circuit shown, the end A is at potential $V_0$ and end B is grounded. The electric current I indicated in the circuit is [a repeating ladder network of resistors: series R, then rungs of R, then 2R sections with rungs of 2R, ending at grounded B]
questions.explanation: The repeating ladder network reduces to an effective resistance $R_{eff}=R+2R=3R$, so $I=\dfrac{V_0}{3R}$.

questions.q: The electric current flowing through a given conductor varies with time as shown in the graph below [current I rises linearly from about 100 mA at t=0 to 400 mA at t=10s, then stays constant at 400 mA up to t=20s]. The number of free electrons which flow through a given cross-section of the conductor in the time interval $0\le t\le20s$ is
questions.explanation: The charge $Q=ne$ equals the area under the I-t graph, which works out to $5\,C$; so $n=\dfrac{5}{1.6\times10^{-19}}=3.125\times10^{19}$.

questions.q: The I-V graph for a conductor at two different temperatures $100^0C$ and $400^0C$ is as shown in the figure [two straight lines through the origin, making angles $45^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ with the V-axis]. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the conductor is about (in per degree Celsius)
questions.explanation: $R_1=\cot45^\circ=1$, $R_2=\cot30^\circ=\sqrt3$; $\alpha=\dfrac{R_2-R_1}{R_1t_2-R_2t_1}\approx3\times10^{-3}\,/^\circ C$.

questions.q: An electric blub of 60 W, 120 V is to be connected to 220 V source. What resistance should be connected in series with the bulb, so that the bulb glows properly?
questions.explanation: Bulb resistance $R=\dfrac{V^2}{P}=240\Omega$, rated current $I=0.5A$; required total resistance $=\dfrac{220}{0.5}=440\Omega$, so the series resistance $=440-240=200\Omega$.

questions.q: A moving electron produces
questions.explanation: A moving charge constitutes a current and produces both an electric field (due to its charge) and a magnetic field (due to its motion).

questions.q: A coil having 9 turns carrying a current produces magnetic filed $B_1$ at the centre. Now the coil is rewounded into 3 turns carrying same current. Then the magnetic field at the centre $B_2=$
questions.explanation: Rewinding the same wire into fewer turns increases the radius proportionally ($r\propto N$); since $B\propto N/r\propto N^2$, reducing N from 9 to 3 (a factor of 1/3) gives $B_2=B_1/9$.

questions.q: A particle of specific charge $\dfrac{q}{m}=\pi\,Ckg^{-1}$ is projected the origin towards positive x-axis with the velocity $10\,ms^{-1}$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec B=-2\hat kT$. The velocity $\vec v$ of particle after time $t=\dfrac{1}{12}s$ will be (in $ms^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: The cyclotron period is $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi\times2}=1\,s$; in $t=\dfrac{1}{12}s=\dfrac{T}{12}$ the velocity turns through $30^\circ$, giving $\vec v=10\cos30^\circ\hat i+10\sin30^\circ\hat j=5(\sqrt3\hat i+\hat j)$.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I is 64 times the magnetic field at a distance x on its axis from the centre of the coil. Then the value of x is
questions.explanation: $B_{centre}=64B_{axis}\Rightarrow(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}=64R^3=(4R)^3\Rightarrow R^2+x^2=16R^2\Rightarrow x=R\sqrt{15}$.

questions.q: A uniform magnetic field of strength $B=2mT$ exists vertically downwards. These magnetic field lines pass through a closed surface as shown in the figure. The closed surface consists of a hemisphere $S_1$, a right circular cone $S_2$ and a circular surface $S_3$ [hemisphere on top and cone below, joined at a common flat circular face $S_3$ of radius $R=10/\sqrt\pi$ cm, with $\vec B$ pointing straight down]. The magnetic flux through $S_1$ and $S_2$ are respectively
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law for magnetism the net flux through any closed surface is zero, so the flux entering through one curved part must equal the flux leaving the other; using $\Phi=B\pi R^2=20\mu Wb$ gives $\Phi_{S_1}=-20\mu Wb,\Phi_{S_2}=+20\mu Wb$ (this question was ambiguous and KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates).

questions.q: In the figure, a conducting ring of certain resistance is falling towards a current carrying straight long conductor. The ring and conductor are in the same plane. Then the [ring A falls vertically towards a horizontal wire B carrying current I to the right]
questions.explanation: As the ring falls closer to the wire, the flux linking it increases, so by Lenz's law the induced current flows clockwise to oppose the increasing flux.

questions.q: An induced current of 2 A flows through a coil. The resistance of the coil is $10\Omega$. What is the change in magnetic flux associated with the coil in 1 ms ?
questions.explanation: $e=iR=2\times10=20\,V=\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}\Rightarrow d\phi=20\times10^{-3}=2\times10^{-2}\,Wb$.

questions.q: A square loop of side length 'a' is moving away from an infinitely long current carrying conductor at a constant speed 'v' as shown. Let 'x' be the instantaneous distance between the long conductor and side AB. The mutual inductance (M) of the square loop - long conductor pair changes with time (t) according to which of the following graphs? [square loop of side a, with side AB at distance x from a long straight current-carrying wire, moving away with speed v]
options: M decreases with a convex curve, approaching the t-axis
M decreases linearly to zero with t
questions.explanation: $M=\dfrac{\mu_0a}{2\pi}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{x+a}{x}\right)$ with $x=x_0+vt$; this decreases in a convex, non-linear way and asymptotically approaches zero as t increases.

questions.q: In an LCR series circuit, the value of only capacitance C is varied. The resulting variation of resonance frequency $f_0$ as a function of C can be represented as [four candidate f0-vs-C graphs: (A) rises then falls, (B) straight line rising, (C) decreasing convex curve, (D) decreasing then rising]
options: a curve that rises and then falls
a straight line increasing with C
a decreasing convex curve approaching the C-axis
a curve that falls and then rises
questions.explanation: $f_0=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt C}$, which is a monotonically decreasing curve as C increases.

questions.q: The figure shows variation of R, $X_L$ and $X_C$ with frequency 'f' in a series LCR circuit [XC falls with frequency, XL rises with frequency, R is a constant horizontal line; points A, B, C, D are marked on the frequency axis in increasing order, with the XL-XC crossing near C/D]. Then for what frequency point is the circuit capacitive?
questions.explanation: The circuit is capacitive when $X_C>X_L$, i.e. at frequencies below the resonance (crossing) point; among the marked points this is point A.

questions.q: The final image formed by an astronomical telescope is
questions.explanation: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment forms a virtual, inverted, and magnified final image.

questions.q: If the angle of minimum deviation is equal to angle of a prism for an equilateral prism, then the speed of light inside the prism is _____
questions.explanation: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+d_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}$; with $A=d_m=60^\circ$, $\mu=\dfrac{\sin60^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt3$, so $v=\dfrac{c}{\mu}=\sqrt3\times10^8\,ms^{-1}$.

questions.q: A luminous point object O is placed at a distance 2R from the spherical boundary separating two transparent media of refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$ as shown, where R is the radius of curvature of the spherical surface. If $n_1=\dfrac43,n_2=\dfrac32$ and R=10cm, the image is obtained at a distance from P equal to [O in medium $n_1$ at distance 2R from the vertex P of a spherical surface curving into medium $n_2$, centre of curvature C beyond P]
questions.explanation: Using $\dfrac{n_2}{v}-\dfrac{n_1}{u}=\dfrac{n_2-n_1}{R}$ with $u=-2R=-20$cm: $\dfrac{3/2}{v}-\dfrac{4/3}{-20}=\dfrac{3/2-4/3}{10}$ gives $v=-30$cm, i.e. 30 cm on the same (rarer, $n_1$) side.

questions.q: An equiconvex lens of radius of curvature 14 cm is made up of two different materials. Left half and right half of vertical portion is made up of material of refractive index 1.5 and 1.2 respectively as shown in the figure. If a point object is placed at a distance of 40 cm, calculate the image distance.
questions.explanation: Each half acts as a thin lens with $f=\dfrac{R}{2(\mu-1)}$; the two halves in parallel give an effective focal length of 20 cm, and $\dfrac1v-\dfrac1u=\dfrac1f$ with $u=-40$cm gives $v=40$cm.

questions.q: Three polaroid sheets are co-axially placed as indicated in the diagram. Pass axes of the polaroids 2 and 3 make $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ with pass axis of polaroid sheet 1. If $I_0$ is the intensity of the incident unpolarised light entering sheet 1, the intensity of the emergent light through sheet 3 is [unpolarised light $I_0$ passes through polaroid 1, then polaroid 2 at $30^\circ$ to polaroid 1's pass axis, then polaroid 3 at $90^\circ$ to polaroid 1's pass axis]
questions.explanation: Intensity after sheet 1 is $I_0/2$; applying Malus's law through sheets 2 and 3 (at $30^\circ$ and then $60^\circ$) gives $I=\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^230^\circ\sin^230^\circ=\dfrac{3I_0}{32}$.

questions.q: Light of energy E falls normally on a metal of work function $\dfrac{E}{3}$. The kinetic energies (K) of the photo electrons are
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy $=E-W_0=E-\dfrac{E}{3}=\dfrac{2E}{3}$; since photoelectrons can lose energy before emission, K ranges from 0 up to $\dfrac{2E}{3}$.

questions.q: The photoelectric work function for photo metal is 2.4 eV. Among the four wavelengths, the wavelength of light for which photo-emission does not take place is
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0=\dfrac{1240}{2.4}\approx517\,nm$; photoemission occurs only for $\lambda\le\lambda_0$, so at 700 nm (longer wavelength, lower photon energy) it does not take place.

questions.q: In alpha particle scattering experiment, if v is the initial velocity of the particle, then the distance of closest approach is d. If the velocity is doubled, then the distance of closest approach becomes
questions.explanation: The distance of closest approach $d\propto\dfrac{1}{v^2}$, so doubling v reduces d to $\dfrac{d}{4}$.

questions.q: The ratio of area of first excited state to ground state of orbit of hydrogen atom is
questions.explanation: Orbit radius $r\propto n^2$, so area $\propto r^2\propto n^4$; for $n=2$ versus $n=1$, the ratio is $2^4:1^4=16:1$.

questions.q: The ratio of volume of $Al^{27}$ nucleus to its surface area is (Given $R_0=1.2\times10^{-15}m$)

Consider the nuclear fission reaction $^1_0n+^{235}_{92}U\rightarrow^{144}_{56}Ba+^{89}_{36}Kr+3^1_0n$. Assuming all the kinetic energy is carried away by the fast neutrons only and total binding energies of $^{235}_{92}U$, $^{144}_{56}Ba$, and $^{89}_{36}Kr$ to be 1800 MeV, 1200 MeV and 780 MeV respectively, the average kinetic energy carried by each fast neutron is (in MeV)
questions.explanation: Energy released $=$ B.E(products) $-$ B.E(reactants) $=(1200+780)-1800=180$ MeV, shared among 3 neutrons, giving 60 MeV each.

questions.q: Depletion region in an unbiased semiconductor diode is a region consisting of
questions.explanation: In the depletion region the electrons and holes have recombined/diffused away, leaving only immobile ions and no free charge carriers.

questions.q: The upper level of valence band and lower level of conduction band overlap in the case of
questions.explanation: Copper is a conductor, in which the valence band and conduction band overlap with no energy gap.

questions.q: A p-n junction diode is connected to a battery of emf 5.7 V in series with a resistant $5k\Omega$ such that it is forward biased. If the barrier potential of the diode is 0.7 V, neglecting the diode resistance, the current in the circuit is
An athlete runs along a circular track of diameter 80m. The distance travelled and the magnitude of displacement of the athlete when he covers $\dfrac{3}{4}^{th}$ of the circle is (in m)
questions.explanation: Distance $=\dfrac34\times2\pi r=\dfrac34\times2\pi(40)=60\pi\,m$; displacement (chord subtending $270^\circ$) $=\sqrt2\,r=40\sqrt2\,m$.

questions.q: Among the given pair of vectors, the resultant of two vectors can never be 3 units. The vectors are
questions.explanation: The resultant of two vectors P and Q always lies between $|P-Q|$ and $P+Q$; for 4 and 8 units this range is 4 to 12, which excludes 3.

questions.q: A block of certain mass is placed on a rough inclined plane. The angle between the plane and the horizontal is $30^0$. The coefficients of static and kinetic frictions between the block and the inclined plane are 0.6 and 0.5 respectively. Then the magnitude of the acceleration of the block is [Take g=10 ms$^{-2}$]
questions.explanation: Maximum static friction $=\mu_smg\cos30^\circ\approx0.52mg$ exceeds the driving force $mg\sin30^\circ=0.5mg$, so the block remains at rest and the acceleration is zero.

questions.q: A particle of mass 500 g is at rest. It is free to move along a straight line. The power delivered to the particle varies with time according to the following graph [P increases linearly from 2 W at t=0 to 8 W at t=5s]. The momentum of the particle at t=5s is
questions.explanation: Work done = area under the P-t graph $=\dfrac{2+8}{2}\times5=25\,J=\dfrac{p^2}{2m}$; with $m=0.5$kg, $p=5\,kg\,m/s$.

questions.q: Dimensional formula for activity of a radioactive substance is
questions.explanation: Activity is the number of decays per unit time, so its dimensional formula is $M^0L^0T^{-1}$.

questions.q: A ceiling fan is rotating around a fixed axle as shown. The direction of angular velocity is along ______ [fan blades rotate in the horizontal (x-y) plane about a vertical axle along z]
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule applied to the fan's sense of rotation as shown, the angular velocity vector points along the negative z-axis.

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg is suspended by a weightless string which passes over a frictionless pulley of mass 2 kg as shown in the figure. The mass is released from a height of 1.6m from the ground. With what velocity does it strike the ground? [a solid pulley of mass 2kg fixed at the top; a string over it holds a 1kg mass 1.6m above the ground]
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: By energy conservation, $m_1gh=\dfrac12m_1V^2+\dfrac12I\omega^2$ with the pulley as a disk ($I=\dfrac12m_2r^2$), giving $1\times10\times1.6=\left(\dfrac12\times1+\dfrac14\times2\right)V^2=V^2$, so $V=4\,ms^{-1}$ (option D); the KEA key accepted both options C and D for this question.

questions.q: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to half the radius of the Earth, from its surface?
A thick metal wire of density $\rho$ and length 'L' is hung from a rigid support. The increase in length of the wire due to its own weight is (Y=Young's modulus of the material of the wire)
questions.explanation: Treating the wire's own weight as acting effectively at its centre, the elongation is $\Delta L=\dfrac{mgL}{2AY}=\dfrac{\rho gL^2}{2Y}$.

questions.q: Water flows through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section at a rate of $0.314\,m^3s^{-1}$. The velocity of water at a point where the radius of the pipe is 10 cm is
questions.explanation: $Q=Av\Rightarrow0.314=\pi(0.1)^2\times v\Rightarrow v=10\,ms^{-1}$.

questions.q: A solid cube of mass m at a temperature $\theta_0$ is heated at a constant rate. It becomes liquid at temperature $\theta_1$ and vapour at temperature $\theta_2$. Let $s_1$ and $s_2$ be specific heats in its solid and liquid states respectively. If $L_f$ and $L_v$ are latent heats of fusion and vaporisation respectively, then the minimum heat energy supplied to the cube until it vaporises is
questions.explanation: Total heat = heating the solid + melting + heating the liquid + vaporising: $Q=ms_1(\theta_1-\theta_0)+mL_f+ms_2(\theta_2-\theta_1)+mL_v$.

questions.q: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is taken round the cyclic process MNOM. The work done by the gas is [P-V diagram: a right triangle with vertices M at $(V_0,3P_0)$, N at $(3V_0,P_0)$, and O at $(V_0,P_0)$]
questions.explanation: Work done equals the area of the triangular cycle $=\dfrac12\times(3V_0-V_0)\times(3P_0-P_0)=2P_0V_0$.
